title: Reciprocity of two normalized polynomials with reciprocal root multisets
statement:
Let $L$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $T$ an indeterminate, and $P,Q\in L[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] polynomials with constant coefficient $P(0)=Q(0)=1$. Put $n=\deg P$, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\in L^\times$ be the reciprocal roots of $P$ counted with multiplicity [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization], so that $P(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}(1-\alpha_rT)$. Let $c\in L^\times$, and suppose that the multiset of reciprocal roots of $Q$ is the image of that of $P$ under $\alpha\mapsto c/\alpha$, that is, $Q(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}(1-c\alpha_r^{-1}T)$ (equivalently: the roots of $Q$ in $L$, with multiplicity, are the $(cz)^{-1}$ for the roots $z$ of $P$). With the coefficient notation $[T^m]$ of [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient], define the determinant constants

$$
D_P=(-1)^{n}[T^{n}]P(T)=\prod_{r=1}^{n}\alpha_r,
\qquad
D_Q=(-1)^{\deg Q}[T^{\deg Q}]Q(T).
$$

Then:

1. $\deg Q=n$, $D_P\neq0$, $D_Q\neq0$, and $D_P\,D_Q=c^{\,n}$.

2. In the Laurent polynomial ring $L[T,T^{-1}]$ [def-weil-laurent-polynomial-ring], with the substitution $T\mapsto c^{-1}T^{-1}$ of [def-weil-rational-function-field],

$$
P(c^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^{n}\,T^{-n}\,D_Q^{-1}\,Q(T).
$$

3. In particular, for every $t\in L^\times$, $P(c^{-1}t^{-1})=t^{-n}\,\bigl([T^{n}]Q\bigr)^{-1}Q(t)$, where $[T^n]Q=(-1)^nD_Q$ is the leading coefficient of $Q$.

source.place: ## Proof, steps 2 and 3: the computations $D_i=\prod\alpha_{i,r}$, $D_{2d-i}=\prod q^d/\alpha_{i,r}=q^{db_i}/D_i$ and $P_{2d-i}(q^{-d}T^{-1})=\prod(1-\alpha_{i,r}^{-1}T^{-1})=(-1)^{b_i}T^{-b_i}(\prod\alpha_{i,r})^{-1}\prod(1-\alpha_{i,r}T)$, stated here for abstract polynomials (the blueprint's $P$ is $P_{2d-i}$, its $Q$ is $P_i$, $c=q^d$). Lean (slopmaster2, no sorry, named by no node before this one): module WeilConjectures.Mathlib.FieldTheory.IsAlgClosed.Basic, Polynomial.leadingCoeff_mul_leadingCoeff_of_roots_eq_map_inv (lines 94-118, clause 1 in the form lc P · lc Q = c^{deg P}) and Polynomial.eval_inv_mul_inv_of_roots_eq_map_inv (lines 120-145, clause 3, the evaluation form of clause 2); the hypothesis there is `Q.roots = P.roots.map fun z ↦ (c * z)⁻¹`.

proof.text: Root factorization and nonvanishing. The cited factorization node supplies elements α₁,…,αₙ∈L× with P(T)=∏ᵣ₌₁ⁿ(1−αᵣT), counted with multiplicity. Thus every αᵣ is nonzero, and the displayed hypothesis already writes Q(T)=∏ᵣ₌₁ⁿ(1−cαᵣ⁻¹T).

source.place: ## Proof, step 2: factorization into reciprocal roots

proof.text: Degree and determinant constants. Each factor 1−αᵣT and 1−cαᵣ⁻¹T has nonzero leading coefficient because αᵣ and c are units. The leading coefficient of a finite product is the product of the leading coefficients, so deg Q=n. Reading the coefficient of Tⁿ in the two displayed products gives D_P=∏ᵣ αᵣ and D_Q=∏ᵣ(cαᵣ⁻¹)=cⁿ(∏ᵣαᵣ)⁻¹. Hence D_P and D_Q are nonzero and D_PD_Q=cⁿ.

source.place: ## Proof, step 2: the computations D_i=∏α_{i,r} and D_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}/D_i

proof.text: Laurent substitution. In L[T,T⁻¹], for each r one has 1−αᵣc⁻¹T⁻¹=−αᵣc⁻¹T⁻¹(1−cαᵣ⁻¹T). Multiplying these n identities and using the product formula for Q yields P(c⁻¹T⁻¹)=(−1)ⁿT⁻ⁿ(∏ᵣαᵣ) c⁻ⁿ Q(T)=(−1)ⁿT⁻ⁿD_Q⁻¹Q(T), where the last equality is the relation D_PD_Q=cⁿ from the preceding step.

Evaluation form. Substituting any t∈L× for T in the Laurent identity is legitimate because t and t⁻¹ exist in the field. It gives P(c⁻¹t⁻¹)=(−1)ⁿt⁻ⁿD_Q⁻¹Q(t). Since [Tⁿ]Q=(−1)ⁿD_Q by the determinant-constant definition, (−1)ⁿD_Q⁻¹=([Tⁿ]Q)⁻¹, and therefore P(c⁻¹t⁻¹)=t⁻ⁿ([Tⁿ]Q)⁻¹Q(t).
